source.title: Theoretical Foundations of Scaling Law in Familial Models
source.authors: Huan Song; Qing-Fei Zhao; Ting Long; Shuyu Tian; Hong-Jun An; Jia-Wei Shao; Chi Zhang; Xue-Long Li

record.file_problem: The paper text appears complete. Some equation coefficients conflict: the coefficient 2980.958 in the introductory version of Equation 2 appears as 2980.058 in the Results and Conclusion.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law experiments to Familial Models, a multi-exit architecture, and reports fitted loss relationships and branch-level results in that new setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for Familial Models, branch losses, a compute-efficient frontier, and an Efficiency Leverage metric. Its text does not specify that the fitted losses are held-out losses. Figure 2's frontier and Figures 3–7 show curves without numerical values in the supplied text; verbal descriptions are recorded where provided. Literature results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study adopts the Chinchilla additive power-law form, adds a granularity factor, fits it to multi-exit runs and uses the fit to derive its own results (gamma, branch penalties, Efficiency Leverage). It does not test whether the power law holds. No goodness-of-fit, residuals, alternative functional forms or quantified extrapolation error are reported. The dense size range is narrow (1B–4B; families up to 12B over 10^19–10^21 FLOPs), so it cannot speak to 'several orders of magnitude'. The measured quantity is training loss averaged across exits, not held-out loss of a single LM. The Huber-delta remark is a one-sentence note on tuning the authors' own fit, with no numbers, so it is not a result on extrapolation or fit-dependence. The compute-efficient frontier is a figure with no allocation exponents.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim three further things: the largest branch matches a same-size dense model within a negligible margin, EL rises with G, and EL is largest at low compute. From these they argue 'train once, deploy many' preserves near compute-optimal scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts IsoFLOP scaling experiments and fitting to a shared-backbone, multi-exit Familial Models architecture, adds granularity and branch-point terms, and reports branch and Efficiency Leverage analyses rather than reproducing the original dense-model measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Huber-loss δ: the authors report that larger values tend to overfit lower-compute regimes and predict held-out larger-compute runs poorly, while δ<10^-3 does not materially change predictions. Branch loss also depends on whether added branches precede or follow the evaluated branch, and the text says the downstream-branch penalty slope decreases as compute increases.

fits_no_version.finding: A Chinchilla-form law with a multiplicative G^0.0333 term fitted to multi-exit (Familial) LM runs; the reported fit has N exponent 0.2982 and D exponent 0.3412, with training loss averaged over exits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average multi-exit LM training loss is fit by an N,D power law with a small granularity penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that a larger Huber delta overfits low-compute runs and predicts larger-compute runs poorly. No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robust-fit hyperparameters affect scaling-law extrapolation in multi-exit models.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream exits penalize a branch's loss far more than upstream exits (fitted coefficients 0.0397 for Q vs 1e-3 for P). The penalty shrinks with compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multi-exit LMs, branch-loss penalties depend on exit position relative to the branch.

fits_no_version.finding: Efficiency Leverage computed from the fitted law is above 1 for G=3–6, increases with G and is largest at low compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Familial Models have lower fitted average loss than size-matched dense sets at equal FLOPs.

record.problems: The text does not establish that empirical loss values are held out; uncertainty intervals are not reported; several results are only visually presented without numerical values in the supplied text; and the D-term coefficient in Equation 2 conflicts between sections.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Values for individual curves in Figures 3–7 are not separately extractable from the supplied text; the reported textual trends and the separate G conditions in Figure 7 are retained.

untested.parts: The power-law form is assumed and fitted. There is no fit quality, no held-out loss and no multi-order-of-magnitude range.
No compute-optimal N/D exponents and no Kaplan vs Hoffmann comparison.
Depth and width at fixed N are not varied as a shape test.
Other modalities and regimes appear only as future-work discussion.
No comparison of exponents across fitting choices. The Huber-delta remark is unquantified.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. The scaling-law form is a tool here, and all headline results (gamma, branch law, EL) are derived from the authors' own fit. Internal inconsistencies: the D coefficient differs between sections; whether the fit uses one group or all runs is contradictory; Table 2 families (2B, 3B, 4B) do not match the families named in the text (fam2B, fam4B, fam8B, fam12B). Figures 3–6 explicitly report training loss. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The reported Familial Models loss fit is not identified as a held-out loss measurement in the text, so it cannot establish the version's held-out pretraining-loss claim.
The text reports a fitting-hyperparameter sensitivity for predictions on held-out larger-compute runs, but does not give a quantified small-run-to-larger-run extrapolation result or the scale gap.

The paper presents a compute-efficient frontier, but the supplied text gives no numerical optimal parameter/token allocations or fitted growth exponents, and does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann allocation trends.
The study varies exit number and placement, not depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count as a general architecture-shape test.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer are discussed as possible future applications, not tested.
No downstream task performance or relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance is tested.

The reported sensitivity concerns the Huber-loss δ choice. The study does not test whether fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations change with parameter counting, data, training schedule, or other fitting methods, nor whether curves bend away from power laws.

rows.subject: Familial Models (aggregate fitted scaling law)
rows.size_stated: Representative dense baselines are 1B, 2B, 3B, and 4B; branch experiments also discuss fam2B, fam4B, fam8B, and fam12B families.
rows.operation_detail: Fit a joint loss function in model size N, training tokens D, and granularity G to experimental runs.

conditions.value: G values shown in Figure 1 are 1, 2, 3, and 4
full set of runs across experimental groups

rows.measure: Fitted loss as a function of N, D, and G
rows.value: The reported fit has E=1.0059, N exponent 0.2982, D exponent 0.3412, and G exponent 0.0333; the D-term coefficient is given as 2980.958 in the introduction and 2980.058 in Results and Conclusion.
rows.note: The text describes a fitted loss scaling law, but does not say that the empirical loss observations are held out. Accordingly, this row is not linked to V1.
rows.check: This is the authors' fitted law, not a test of the power-law form: there is no fit-quality measure and no alternative form, and the data are training losses averaged over exits. The text also conflicts on what was fitted: Sec 4.1 says 'for the representative experimental group', while Sec 3.3 says fits use the full set of runs. The D coefficient is 2980.958 vs 2980.058.

rows.subject: Familial Models (compute-efficient frontier)
rows.operation_detail: Plot the implied compute-optimal allocation of model size for training budgets.

conditions.value: varying FLOPs budgets; experimental budgets elsewhere in the paper range from 10^19 to 10^21 FLOPs

rows.measure: Compute-efficient frontier relating model size and data scale
rows.note: The caption says the line represents compute-optimal model size for a given training budget. The supplied text does not provide the curve values or describe a power-law trend.
rows.check: Figure-only frontier derived from the fitted law. No optimal N or D exponents or numerical allocation are given, so it cannot bear on V3. It should not be linked to V3.

rows.subject: Familial Models (aggregate scaling-law fit)
rows.operation_detail: Compare fit and larger-compute prediction behavior under different Huber-loss δ choices.

conditions.value: δ=10^-3 used; larger δ and δ<10^-3 discussed

rows.measure: Effect of fitting-loss choice on fitted behavior and prediction of larger-compute runs
rows.baseline: δ=10^-3; predictions with δ<10^-3 are stated not to change materially
rows.value: Larger δ tends to overfit lower-compute regimes and predict held-out larger-compute runs poorly; δ<10^-3 does not materially change predictions.
rows.locator: Section 3.2, Robust objective: Huber loss on log-residuals
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative fitting-sensitivity result but no numerical prediction errors or exponents for the alternative fits.
rows.check: This is a qualitative hyperparameter-tuning note for the authors' own fitting procedure (choosing Huber delta), not a measured extrapolation result. No prediction errors, no held-out runs identified, no scale gap and no alternative exponents are given. It should not be linked to V2 or V7, and 'partial' is not a readable state.

conditions.value: varied; exact curve values are not stated

rows.baseline: Independently trained dense models of matching parameter count
rows.value: The text says training loss increases monotonically with G, with an approximately linear relationship.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative trend; the figure's individual values are not provided.
rows.check: Subject list mentions fam8B and fam12B, which are not in Table 2 (which lists 2B, 3B and 4B families). The measure is training loss, not held-out loss.

rows.subject: Familial Models second-branch models: 1B in fam2B, 2B in fam4B, 4B in fam8B, and 6B in fam12B
rows.operation_detail: Compare second-branch training loss across granularity settings and matched-size dense models.

conditions.value: G=1 to 2, then G≥2; exact curve values are not stated

rows.baseline: Independently trained dense models of matching parameter count
rows.value: The text says increasing G from 1 to 2 incurs only a marginal loss penalty; for G≥2, loss returns to a near-linear trend with G.
rows.note: The reported response depends on whether added branches are upstream or downstream of the evaluated branch.
rows.check: The state should describe the reported pattern, which the text states: marginal penalty from G=1 to 2, then near-linear. 'Partial' has no version to be partial against.

rows.subject: Familial Models branch models (aggregate fit over experimental configurations)
rows.operation_detail: Fit branch loss as a function of preceding and succeeding branch points and token budget.

conditions.value: dense model with matched parameter count and compute

rows.measure: Branch loss relative to matched dense-model loss
rows.baseline: L_dense for a dense model with matched parameter count and compute
rows.value: Fitted relation: L=L_dense+1×10^-3·P+0.0397·Q·(2.75×10^6/D)^0.5734; the text says added preceding branches have much smaller impact than following branches.
rows.note: P counts preceding branch points and Q counts succeeding branch points.

rows.measure: Efficiency Leverage, defined as dense average loss divided by Familial Models average loss
rows.baseline: EL=1 is the equality point implied by the stated ratio
rows.value: Figure only; the text states EL is consistently greater than 1 across the granularities and compute budgets considered.
rows.note: The reported value is computed from the fitted scaling law, not described as a direct measurement of independent raw losses.
rows.check: EL is computed from the fitted law, not from measured losses. This is the study's own derived metric.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report that larger δ tends to overfit lower-compute regimes and predict held-out larger-compute runs poorly; this is a qualitative sensitivity result, not a quantified small-to-large extrapolation test (r3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported fit and larger-compute prediction behavior changes with this fitting choice, although the sensitivity is only described qualitatively (r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors say reducing δ below 10^-3 does not materially change predictions, so the reported fitting sensitivity is not universal across the tested δ choices (r3).
